title: Emit structured data as JSON-LD that parses without error
statement: Every script element declaring the JSON-LD media type contains a document that parses as JSON, declares an @context, and gives every node an @type drawn from the vocabulary.
rationale: A block that fails to parse is discarded whole, so the markup contributes nothing while still appearing in the page source, which makes the failure invisible to anyone reading the template rather than the response.
implementation: Build the object in code and serialise it with a JSON serialiser rather than assembling the string in a template, and escape any closing script sequence the serialised text may contain. Validate the serialised output during the build so a malformed block fails there.

verification.method: Extract every JSON-LD script block from the served response, parse each one, and record the parse result alongside the node types found.

sources.title: JSON-LD 1.1: A JSON-based Serialization for Linked Data

title: Keep structured data consistent with the content visible on the page
statement: Every value asserted in the markup - name, price, availability, date, author, rating, breadcrumb trail - is also present in the visible content of the same page and says the same thing.
rationale: Markup describing something the page does not show is treated as misleading under published guidelines, and the mismatch is what triggers manual action rather than the markup simply being ignored.
implementation: Generate the markup from the same data the template renders, in the same request, so the two cannot diverge. Never populate a property from a default, a placeholder, or a value fetched separately from the one displayed.

verification.method: For each asserted property, search the visible text of the same response for the value and report properties whose value does not appear.

sources.title: General structured data guidelines, content guidelines

title: Use the most specific schema type that truthfully describes the page
statement: A node's @type is the narrowest vocabulary type whose definition the page actually satisfies, and it is not widened to a generic type nor narrowed to one whose required properties the page cannot honestly supply.
rationale: The type declares what kind of thing the page is about, so a type the page does not satisfy misstates the subject, and a type too generic to carry the properties the content has discards information the vocabulary could express.
implementation: Read the vocabulary definition of the candidate type and confirm the page satisfies it before using it. Where a subtype exists but the page lacks the properties that make it meaningful, choose the parent type instead of inventing values to qualify for the subtype.

verification.method: List the declared node types per route template and compare each against the vocabulary definition and the content the template renders.

sources.title: Getting started with schema.org using microdata and JSON-LD

title: Use absolute canonical URLs inside structured data
statement: Every url, @id, contentUrl, thumbnailUrl, and image value in the markup is an absolute URL on the production origin, and page-level url values match the page's canonical.
rationale: A relative or origin-inconsistent value cannot be resolved reliably outside the page it appeared in, so the node it identifies cannot be matched against the same node referenced from another page.
implementation: Resolve every URL-valued property through the same builder that produces canonical values, so the origin comes from configuration once. Do not emit a path-only value on the assumption the consumer will resolve it against the document address.

verification.method: Collect all URL-valued properties from the parsed markup and report any that lack a scheme and host or whose host differs from the production origin.

sources.title: General structured data guidelines, technical guidelines

title: Claim only the rich result features the platform currently documents
statement: Markup added in order to obtain an enhanced result targets a feature that appears in the platform's current documented feature list, and it supplies every property that feature's documentation marks as required.
rationale: A type valid in the vocabulary is not automatically a supported result feature, and markup for an undocumented or retired feature adds maintenance surface while producing nothing the platform will act on.
implementation: Before adding a feature-targeted block, open the current feature documentation and copy its required property list into the generator as an explicit contract. Record which documented feature each generator targets so a retired feature can be found later.

verification.method: For each feature-targeted block, compare the emitted property set against the required property list in the referenced documentation.

caution: Supplying the documented required properties makes a page eligible for consideration. It does not make an enhanced result appear, and the documented feature list changes over time, which is why this record carries a short review interval.

sources.title: Explore structured data markup that Google Search supports

title: Avoid emitting conflicting objects for the same entity
statement: A page does not describe one thing twice with different values; where several blocks reference the same entity they share an @id and agree on every property they both assert.
rationale: Two descriptions of one thing force the consumer to pick between them, so a stale duplicate left behind by a second plugin or a legacy template can override the values the current template computes.
implementation: Compose one graph per page from a single generator and emit it in one block, rather than letting each component contribute its own block. Where a plugin adds markup you cannot remove, disable its output instead of emitting a second competing description.

verification.method: Group the parsed nodes by type and identifier and report groups holding more than one node with differing property values.

title: Render structured data in the server response
statement: The JSON-LD block is present in the response body as delivered, rather than injected by client script after load, and the block present after hydration is identical to the one delivered.
rationale: Markup that only exists after script execution is absent from the response any consumer reads without rendering, and a block written twice by server and client produces two competing descriptions of the same entity.
implementation: Emit the block from the server render path alongside the content it describes. If a client-side library currently injects it, remove that injection rather than leaving both in place, and compute the values on the server from the same data the page renders.

verification.method: Diff the JSON-LD blocks found in the unexecuted response body against those present in the hydrated document.

title: Derive review and rating markup only from real collected reviews
statement: Every review, rating, and aggregate rating property is computed from reviews the site actually holds and displays, and no such property is emitted for an item that has received none.
rationale: Rating markup that is not backed by collected reviews is fabricated data about a real-world subject, which is prohibited by published policy and cannot be corrected later by editing the number.
implementation: Read the count and average from the review store at render time and omit the whole property when the count is zero. An automated agent must not create, seed, estimate, or default any review or rating value, and must report the absence instead.

verification.method: Trace each emitted rating value back to the stored review records it summarises and report any value with no records behind it.
